title: Personal Data Disclosure in the Case of Ms Sua Li Li
what_it_is: Personal Data Disclosure in the Case of Ms Sua Li Li

sections.label: Disclosure to counter inaccuracies
sections.summary: Government agencies may disclose personal data to counter inaccuracies in publicised complaints or petitions about Government processes or policies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To recap, Government agencies may disclose personal data to counter inaccuracies about the Government’s processes or policies contained in publicised complaints or petitions.

sections.label: Public clarification in Ms Sua's case
sections.summary: Five Government agencies issued a public clarification to provide omitted facts and correct misleading statements in a TOC article.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In Ms Sua's case, a public clarification was issued by the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB), the Housing and Development Board, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Social and Family Development to provide key facts that had been omitted from, and to correct misleading statements in the article first published by The Online Citizen (TOC) on 17 December 2019.

sections.label: Pseudonym use and Ms Sua's identity
sections.summary: Continued use of the pseudonym could confuse the public and was not meaningful as Ms Sua had already divulged her identity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Continued use of the pseudonym, "Ms Soo", could have done more harm than good if the public had associated other individuals with the case, resulting in more confusion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In any case, the continued use of a pseudonym would not have been meaningful to protect Ms Sua's identity as she had already divulged her identity by forwarding her email to the President containing her full name and National Registration Identity Card number to several Government agencies, media outlets and TOC.

sections.label: No public interest in falsehood
sections.summary: No public interest is served by protecting a falsehood about Government processes and policies on social welfare and medical care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Well, I would put it to Ms Anthea Ong that there is no public interest served by protecting a falsehood about Government processes and policies when it comes to social welfare and medical care.

sections.label: Public interest in being informed
sections.summary: The public interest served is for the public to be well-informed about what is actually happening in Government processes and policies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The public interest served here is for the public to be well-informed about what is actually happening in our Government's processes and policies.

sections.label: Initial disclosure by Ms Sua and TOC
sections.summary: The disclosure was made initially by Ms Sua and TOC.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If I understand the timeline correctly, that disclosure was made initially by Ms Sua and TOC.

sections.label: Facts already public domain
sections.summary: The facts Ms Anthea Ong refers to were already public when the clarification was issued.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The facts that Ms Anthea Ong is referring to were already in the public domain at the time that the clarification was issued.
